title: Close overtakes admitted request construction
issue: A send can pass the open check and pause while constructing its request. Graceful close could drain an empty strategy and destroy it before that send registers.
change: Admit under the lifecycle monitor before construction. Graceful shutdown waits for admitted construction before draining the strategy.

title: Abort reports completion while construction is held
issue: Abort should start cleanup promptly, but held request construction still belongs to the client. Reporting successful termination at that point loses track of it.
change: Start abort cleanup without waiting for construction, then wait for outstanding operations before publishing successful termination. A failed cleanup remains FAILED, not a claim of release.

title: Response mapping outlives graceful drain
issue: The transport response can be ready while conversion to the public Result is still blocked. Strategy counters alone do not cover that work.
change: Retain the operation through internal resolution and public result publication. This does not promise to wait for arbitrary user continuations on caller-owned threads.

title: Cancelling the public result hides transport work
issue: A caller can cancel its result before the underlying transport operation resolves. Using only isDone would remove that operation too early.
change: Require internal resolution as well as public completion before dropping ownership. Cancellation of the public future does not itself stop the transport.
code:
result.cancel(false);
// Ownership remains until internal resolution.

title: A construction exception strands admission
issue: If request construction throws after admission, a missing discharge would leave shutdown waiting on work that will never register.
change: Publish the failure and run registration cleanup in finally, including synchronous failures.

title: Abort cannot interrupt a graceful drain
issue: A later abort request could leave the first closer waiting in an unconditional graceful drain. Repeated graceful requests must also not reverse an abort.
change: Share the lifecycle state and let the drain loop observe escalation. Only the first request starts cleanup.

title: A progress thread waits for its own shutdown
issue: A result callback, cleanup owner, dispatcher or result-policy callback can block on shutdown that needs that same thread to continue.
change: Reject a blocking wait from known progress-owning threads while shutdown is unfinished. closeAsync initiates shutdown without waiting; an independent thread can await the shared handle.

title: A second destroy returns before cleanup finishes
issue: An atomic started flag prevents duplicate cleanup, but it does not make later callers wait for the first caller’s cleanup result.
change: Keep one destruction result. Repeated callers join it and observe the same success or failure.

title: A cleanup failure disappears for later callers
issue: Without a retained outcome, a later observer can miss an earlier cleanup failure.
change: Publish FAILED with the original cause. Repeated waits report that failure; FAILED does not mean every resource was released.

title: Transport close skips worker cleanup when it throws
issue: A transport-close exception could skip shutdown of the result executor or the reset-accounting executor.
change: Use finally blocks to attempt both executor cleanups even when transport close throws. The injected tests check that the captured workers exit and the failure remains visible.

title: Cleanup waits while holding the accounting monitor
issue: Reset-accounting tasks need the same monitor that close previously held while awaiting their executor. That wait could prevent those tasks from finishing.
change: Release the monitor before waiting for executor termination. Existing reset and shutdown tests exercise the surrounding path; this case still needs a dedicated ordered regression.

title: Success is reported before dispatcher exit
issue: Closing shared resources does not establish that a dispatcher paused elsewhere has stopped.
change: Join the dispatcher after shared cleanup on the successful path, avoiding self-join. The test holds the dispatcher, verifies the shutdown wait remains pending, then releases it.

title: A capacity waiter resumes after abort
issue: An operation registered before abort can be waiting for a slot. When capacity becomes available, it must not start new work after cleanup.
change: Check the abort flag while waiting and again before acquisition. Discharge the unacquired registration when acquisition fails. The check and increment are still separate operations; broader interleavings remain to be checked.

title: The dispatch loop sends queued work after abort
issue: After a held dispatch returns, the inner loop could continue taking requests that were already queued when abort began.
change: Check the abort flag before polling for the next queued request. The test holds the first dispatch, queues another, aborts, then checks that the queued request is not sent. This is not an atomic guarantee across a concurrent check-and-poll race.

title: An observer interferes with shared shutdown
issue: A timeout or interruption should end only that caller’s wait. Observation should not initiate shutdown or cancel another caller’s cleanup.
change: Expose a read-only shared handle. The blocking close wrapper restores the interrupt flag; independent observers can still await the same shutdown.

title: A snapshot reports contradictory state
issue: A public snapshot could claim success while retaining outstanding work, or attach a failure to a non-failed phase.
change: Validate phase, failure and ownership counts at construction. FAILED may retain outstanding work; TERMINATED may not.
